faq_answers.faq_who_lists_market_sale: On the market-sale path, a licensed real estate partner in your market lists the house. Fair and Simple Home Offer is not a licensed real estate agent or brokerage.
faq_answers.faq_show_price_math: Yes. Your offer comes in writing. It shows what you cover (your mortgage payoff, property taxes, liens, and judgments) and shows that we cover the remaining closing costs, which are already built into the number.
faq_answers.faq_who_calls: Someone from our acquisition team usually calls within 1–3 minutes. They may ask for a few photos. Most of the time, we can buy the house without walking through it.
faq_answers.faq_see_inside: Usually not, especially if the house is vacant. Most of the time we go by what you tell us about its condition. On tighter deals, we may ask for photos or more detail first.
faq_answers.faq_offer_negotiable: Once we're under contract, the price stays the same in most cases. It changes only if an inspection turns up problems that weren't disclosed.
faq_answers.faq_offer_duration: Your offer stays open for 3 days, because we're always reviewing other homes too.
faq_answers.faq_proceeds_amounts: We cover the closing costs for the sale. Anything already owed on the property is paid from your proceeds at closing: your mortgage, property taxes, liens, judgments, code violations, and other encumbrances.
faq_answers.faq_how_liens_paid: They're paid off from your proceeds at closing, and each one is listed on your closing breakdown.
faq_answers.faq_underwater_loan: We can't handle short sales because we aren't licensed agents, but we work with partners who can. Ask your acquisition rep about those connections.
faq_answers.faq_payment_method: You choose at signing: a same-day wire, or a check sent overnight that arrives the next day.
faq_answers.faq_tenants_stay: It depends on the situation, so ask your acquisition rep. We'll need to be in touch with the tenants directly, and in some cases we can offer relocation help.
faq_answers.faq_stay_after_closing: It's not typical, but we look at it case by case. Our priority is fitting the closing around your move.
faq_answers.faq_probate_open: Generally, no. Probate is what produces the estate documents needed to sell. In some states, the property can be distributed sooner if all heirs agree.
faq_answers.faq_who_handles_file: Besides Andrew, our operations team of Kaylin, Connor, and Taylor works with sellers and checks in on every file daily.
faq_answers.faq_moving_or_advance: Yes. We can help with moving, and we can provide cash before closing. Just bring it up early, before contracts are signed, and we'll work out the details together.

groups.title: Cash offer vs listing with an agent

items.q: Should I take a cash offer or list my house with an agent?
items.a:
You do not have to pick before we talk. We show a cash offer and a market-sale option, and we compare both with a traditional listing.

Cash is on your timeline. A market sale is usually 45–90 days. A traditional listing is often 3–6 months or more, often about 6% commission, and the seller typically pays some closing costs. Those are typical industry figures. On our two paths, commission is none and we cover closing costs.

items.q: What's the difference between your cash offer and your market-sale option?
items.a:
A cash offer is us buying the house. The market-sale option takes longer and can net more. We do not charge a commission or closing costs on that path either.

Cash is on your timeline, and a market sale is usually 45–90 days. The footer says we are not a licensed brokerage unless stated, and that we buy as principals.

items.q: Why is a cash offer lower than what my house might list for?
items.a:
A cash price is usually below a list price because it has to cover repairs, carrying the house, and the chance it takes time to sell again.

This page will not quote a percent of retail. If cash is not your best result, the market-sale option may put more in your pocket, on a slower clock of about 45–90 days.

items.q: Will you show me how you got to your number?
How do I compare your offer to what I'd net with an agent?
items.a:
Compare what you would receive, not the headline price.

Line up price, commission, closing costs, repairs, and any payoff the title company sends to a lender. On our cash offer and our market-sale path, commission is none and we cover closing costs. A traditional listing often includes about 6% commission and some seller closing costs. Those are typical industry figures, not a quote.

items.q: I'm already listed with a Realtor. Can I still talk to you?
items.a:
Yes. You can still talk to us if the house is already listed. The form does not turn listed homes away.

The form does not cancel a listing agreement. What that agreement allows is a question for your agent or a real estate attorney. We are not attorneys and will not tell you to break a contract. We will still walk through a cash offer or a market-sale option.

items.q: What happens after I submit my address?
items.a:
The form takes about 60 seconds and does not obligate you to sell. The consent box starts unchecked. You do not have to check it, and leaving it blank does not block the form.

You can also call or text (910) 636-6669. There is no purchase-price question. Which property types continue is answered below.

items.q: Do you need to see the inside of the house?
Is the offer negotiable? Does it ever change after a walkthrough or inspection?
How long is an offer good for?
Can a family member or my attorney be part of the conversation?
items.a:
Yes. A family member or your attorney can join the conversation.

Call or text (910) 636-6669 and say who should be included. We are not attorneys. If someone should read the paperwork, that is their job. There is no fee to start, you can say no, and an offer does not obligate you.

items.q: Who pays closing costs, and are there any costs I'd still pay?
items.a:
We cover closing costs on the cash offer and on the market-sale path. We do not charge a commission on either path.

A traditional listing is different: the seller typically pays some closing costs, and commission is often about 6%. Those are typical industry figures, not your quote. A mortgage payoff goes to the lender. It is not a fee we add.

items.q: What happens to my mortgage when I sell?
items.a:
If you still have a mortgage, the loan is paid from the sale at closing. You do not keep the loan and hand us the house.

The title company sends the payoff to your lender. We can help coordinate that. We cannot make the lender pause a case or change the loan. If a foreclosure sale date is in play, the closing has to land in time for a sale to matter.

items.q: Can you buy a house with liens, judgments, or back taxes?
items.a: Yes, we consider houses with liens, judgments, or back taxes. That is already how we describe the houses we look at.

items.q: What if I owe more than the house is worth?
items.a: If a foreclosure date is involved, talk with a foreclosure attorney or a HUD-approved counselor. We are not attorneys.

items.q: Will I owe capital gains tax when I sell?
items.a: Capital gains taxes aren't paid up front at closing. They're handled with the IRS when you file for the year you sell. Talk to a CPA about your situation.

items.q: How do I get paid at closing?
items.a: A title company handles the closing. If there is a mortgage, that company sends the payoff to the lender.

items.q: What types of properties do you buy?
items.a:
We buy single-family houses and multi-family properties with 2–4 units, from the owner.

Townhouses, condos, mobile or manufactured homes, apartments, and vacant land get a short, quiet screen instead of an offer. A listed house is not rejected. The form does not ask for a purchase price. Wholesalers, investors, and agents should not use the owner form.

items.q: What does "as-is" actually mean?
items.a:
As-is means you do not repair or clean the house for us.

Leave what you do not want, including a bad roof, fire damage, or a house that needs a lot of work. We will not ask you to paint, haul junk, or get it ready for showings. What you must disclose is a legal question for an attorney.

items.q: Can I sell a house with tenants in it?
items.a: You can ask us about a rental. Tired landlords are already one of the situations we talk about.

items.q: Can I stay in the house for a while after closing?
Do I need to disclose problems with the house?
items.a:
Do not use this page as the list of what you must disclose.

Disclosure rules depend on the state and the facts. An attorney can tell you what has to be in writing. Tell us about problems you know so the conversation is about the real house. We are not attorneys, and we will not hand you a form and call it legal advice.

items.q: Is it too late to sell if I've got a foreclosure sale date?
items.a:
A sale date does not, by itself, mean it is too late. It also does not mean a sale will stop the foreclosure.

A sale helps only when there is time and the numbers work. We do not promise that foreclosure stops, or anything about your credit. Lender, counselor, cash, and market-sale options are on the stop foreclosure page. For legal advice, use a foreclosure attorney or a HUD-approved counselor at hud.gov/counseling. We are not attorneys.

items.q: Will selling hurt or help my credit?
items.a:
We will not tell you that selling helps your credit, or that it saves it.

We do not know what a lender will report. A sale is not a credit-repair product. If you are worried about a foreclosure on your record, a HUD-approved housing counselor or a foreclosure attorney can talk through that. We are neither.

items.q: Can I sell an inherited house that's still in probate?
items.a: Inherited houses are a common reason people call.

items.q: What if I'm going through a divorce, or co-owners disagree?
items.a:
We can talk with you. We cannot settle a dispute between owners.

If a spouse, heir, or other co-owner has to sign, that is a question for an attorney. We will not tell one owner to sign over someone else's rights. The other owner, or your attorney, can be on the call. There is no fee to ask, and no obligation to sell.

items.q: How can I tell a legitimate cash buyer from a scam?
items.a:
See who you are dealing with before you sign anything.

Fair & Simple Home Offer is operated by Andrew Collier LLC. The footer says we buy as principals and are not a licensed brokerage unless stated. Use (910) 636-6669 and offer@fairandsimplehomeoffer.com. Read the contract, compare it with another option, and open the BBB profile linked from the site. This page does not claim star ratings.

items.q: Will you pressure me or keep calling?
items.a:
You should not be pushed, and you can say no.

The consent box is optional, unchecked, and the form still submits if you leave it blank. Consent is not required to get an offer. We are not publishing how often anyone will call. There is no fee to hear an offer, and hearing it does not obligate you to accept it.

items.q: Who will I actually be working with?
items.a: Andrew Collier is the owner and the public face of the company. More about him is on the Our Company page.

items.q: Can you help with moving or getting cash before closing?
What do I need to have ready to sell?
items.a:
To start, you need the address and a way for us to reach you. You do not need to clean or repair first.

The form asks for your name, the property address, phone, and email. It does not ask for a price. If you go forward, the title company tells you which documents it needs. Bring a co-owner's questions, or your attorney's, to the conversation. Do not put account numbers in the form.
